a.make: In {create}, choose a type, for example Website. Then fill in the content and choose a design. You immediately see how it looks on a phone. Done? Download your code as PNG, SVG, PDF or another format. You'll also find it in {codes}.
a.types: There are 32 types, from a website or PDF to a menu, coupon or Wi-Fi. You see them all in the first step of Create QR Code.
a.edit:
Yes. Most types put a short link in the QR code. If you change the content, the code stays the same and you don’t need to print anything again.
Exception: Wi-Fi and vCard. Their content is inside the code itself, so after a change you use the new code.
a.format: You can download PNG, JPG, SVG, PDF and EPS. PNG and JPG are normal images, handy for websites, email, Word and PowerPoint. SVG, PDF and EPS always stay sharp, however large you make them. Choose those for print, such as flyers, posters and packaging.
a.scanFix:
Make sure there is enough contrast between the code and the background: dark on light works best. Print the code at least 2 by 2 cm, and larger if people scan from further away.
Keep a logo small and leave some space around the code. Always test your code with your own phone before printing.
a.pause:
Yes. In My QR Codes, switch the code off. Anyone who scans it then sees a friendly message that it’s not available right now.
Switch it back on whenever you like. The scans so far are kept.
a.stats: For one code or all your codes together: the number of scans and unique visitors, per day, per system (such as iPhone or Android), per country and per city. Choose the period yourself and download everything as CSV for Excel.
a.privacy: No. We only store counts per day, with the system, country and city. We only use the IP address briefly to work out the country. It is not stored, and people who scan don’t get cookies.
a.location: Country and city are an estimate based on the internet address; they are never a person’s exact location. IP addresses are not stored.
a.password:
Go to My Account > Security and enter your current and new password. You’ll then be logged out on your other devices.
You choose the app language in My Account > Preferences.
a.billing: Go to My Account > Billing details. Choose Company or Private person and fill in your details. A VAT number is optional.
a.data:
In My Account > My data you can download everything we store about you. You can also delete your account there.
Note: this erases all your QR codes, files and analytics, and printed codes stop working.
a.price: Standard costs €4.99, Pro €12.99 and Business €24.99 per month. Paying per quarter is cheaper, and paying yearly gives you 2 months free in the first year. Every plan starts with 14 days free. You see your plan in {acc} > {plan}.
a.unique:
Scans: every time someone scans your QR code, it counts. If one person scans three times, that is 3 scans.
Unique scans: how many different people scanned. Each person counts only once a day per QR code. So those three scans by the same person on one day are 1 unique scan.
Example: 10 customers scan your menu, and 2 of them scan it again later. You then see 12 scans and 10 unique scans.
We recognise a person without cookies and without storing IP addresses, only as a temporary count per day.
a.dynamic:
A dynamic QR code contains a short link to us. That's why you can always change the destination, even after printing, and we count the scans.
Wi-Fi and vCard are deliberately static: they work without internet, but don't count scans and can't be changed after printing.
a.size:
At least about 2 × 2 cm for close-range scanning. Rule of thumb: the code is about a tenth of the scanning distance (so about 30 cm at 3 metres).
Leave an empty margin around the code and always test with two phones before printing.
a.trial: Yes. Every plan starts with 14 days free, including Business. You choose a payment method when you start; cancel within the 14 days and you pay nothing. There is one trial per customer.
a.cancel: Go to {acc} > {plan} > Manage subscription and choose Cancel subscription. Your plan keeps running until the end of the period you paid for. You can also email support@optimasys.es.
a.downgrade: Nothing is deleted. If you have more QR codes than the new plan allows, you choose which ones stay active. The others are paused and work again as soon as you upgrade or buy an extra QR code.
a.many: Yes, on Pro and Business. In {codes}, click {bulk}, download the sample file, fill it in in Excel and choose it. You create up to 500 codes at a time and download them all as one ZIP.
a.api: Yes, with the API in Business. Create a key in {acc} > {api}. Your software can then create, change and pause QR codes and fetch statistics.
a.team: Yes. On Pro you work with up to 3 people, on Business with as many as you like. Invite colleagues in {acc} > {team} as editor or viewer.

privacy.title: Privacy policy
privacy.intro: This policy explains which data QR-Codex processes, why, how long we keep it and what your rights are. We collect as little as possible: no ads, no tracking, and we never sell data.
privacy.s1: QR-Codex is a service of {company}. We are responsible for processing the data of your account. Questions about privacy? Email {email}.
privacy.s2:
**Your account**
- name, email address, profile photo and time zone (if you add them)
- your password, stored only in unreadable form (hashed)
- billing details, if you add them (company name, address, VAT number)
- if you sign in with Google: your name and email address from your Google account
- API keys (Business): only in unreadable form, never the key itself

**Your QR codes**
- the content you enter and the files you upload (photos, PDFs, audio, video), because they are needed to show the page
- passwords of protected codes and Wi-Fi passwords are stored encrypted

**Security**
- for each signed-in device: browser, system, shortened IP address (last part removed) and when it was last active
- recent activity: sign-ins (including failed attempts), password or email changed, signing out other devices

**Scans of your QR codes**
- per code per day only counts per system (for example iOS or Android), country and city
- country and city are looked up in our own database on our server; the visitor's IP address is not stored and not passed on (IP Geolocation by DB-IP, db-ip.com, CC BY 4.0)
- "unique scans" are counted without cookies, using a daily code that can no longer be traced after that day
- for each scan also a line in the log: time, approximate place (city, region, country), system, browser, device and whether it is a new visitor; never the IP address or who it was

**The chat assistant**
- if you use the chat (bottom right), your messages and any details you enter (such as name, email or phone number) are sent to the chat service of {company}
- to pre-fill the phone number field, the chat looks up your country via ipapi.co, which sees your IP address for this
- the chat remembers your conversation in your browser, so you can continue it later
privacy.s3:
- to provide the service: your account, your QR codes and the pages visitors see (performance of the contract)
- to secure your account and the service and prevent abuse (legitimate interest)
- to show statistics about your own codes (legitimate interest)
- to create and keep invoices if you have a paid plan (legal obligation)
privacy.s4:
- your account and QR codes: until you delete them or close your account
- if your subscription ends: your QR codes stop working and are deleted after 30 days
- recent activity: 90 days
- log of individual scans: just over a year (400 days)
- signed-in devices: until you sign out or the session expires
- accounts that were never confirmed: 7 days
- backups: up to 14 days
- invoices: as long as the law requires
- which version of the Terms you accepted, and when: as long as you have an account
privacy.s5:
Only you and, when needed for support or security, the {company} team. We only use parties that are needed to provide the service, such as the hosting provider and (if configured) the service that sends our emails. We make agreements with them about the security of your data. Address lookups for QR codes go through our own server, so the address service does not see you. Payments are processed by our payment provider, Stripe. Our servers are in the European Union. The chat assistant runs on the chat service of {company} (webchat-api.optimasys.es); to find your country it uses ipapi.co.

If you buy as a business, we check your VAT number with VIES, the VAT number check of the European Commission, and Stripe calculates the VAT (Stripe Tax). If you connect your own domain (Business), we register that domain with Cloudflare so it gets a secure certificate. To warn you about broken links, our server visits the destination links of your QR codes once a day; no personal data of visitors is involved.

The pages of your QR codes are public to anyone who scans the code or has the link. Only put information there that may be public.
privacy.s6:
You can view, change and download your data, and delete your account with everything in it. You can do this yourself in My account (Profile and My data). You can also object to processing. For anything you can't do yourself, email {email}; we reply within a month.

Don't agree with how we handle your data? You can file a complaint with the data protection authority in your country. In Spain this is the Agencia Española de Protección de Datos (www.aepd.es).
privacy.s7: QR-Codex is meant for people aged 18 and over. Younger people may only use it with the permission and supervision of a parent or guardian. We do not knowingly collect data from children without that permission; if we find out, we delete the data.
privacy.s8:
- all connections use HTTPS
- passwords are hashed, sensitive content is encrypted
- in My account you can see where you are signed in and sign out any device
- a backup is made every night
privacy.s9: If we change this policy, you can see it from the date at the top. For major changes we will let you know in advance.

cookies.title: Cookies and storage
cookies.intro: QR-Codex only uses what is needed to make the app work. No tracking, advertising or analytics cookies. That is why we don't ask for consent with a cookie banner.
cookies.s1: One cookie, "sid", remembers that you are signed in. Only our server can read it (not scripts), it is only sent over a secure connection and it disappears when you sign out. Without this cookie you cannot sign in.
cookies.s2:
In your browser's storage (localStorage) we only keep your preferences:
- language
- appearance (light or dark) and background
- whether the sidebar is collapsed

In the online demo without a server, your sample codes are also only stored in your browser.
cookies.s3: People who scan a QR code get no cookies from us. We count scans without cookies; see the privacy policy.
cookies.s4: Links to other services (for example Google Maps, WhatsApp or Instagram) are ordinary links. Only when you click them do you go to that service, and their rules apply.
